title: Triclosan and triclocarban-induced spleen injury: insights from network toxicology and weaned piglet models
content:
Abstract
Triclosan (TCS) and triclocarban (TCC) are broad-spectrum antimicrobial agents whose potential impacts on the environment and health have aroused widespread concern. Although their ecotoxicity has been studied, research on their effects on spleen injury is relatively limited. In this study, the effects of TCS and TCC on the spleen of weaned piglets were systematically evaluated by combining network toxicology analysis, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments. Network toxicology analysis identified 67 potential targets and 10 core genes related to spleen injury for TCS, and 167 potential targets and 10 core genes for TCC. Molecular docking revealed significant binding affinity between TCS and TCC and the core target proteins, implying potential damage. In vivo studies showed that high doses of TCS and TCC significantly reduced antioxidant capacity and induced obvious pathological damage in spleen tissue. qRT-PCR analysis showed upregulation of some core target genes, further confirming the damaging effects of TCS and TCC on the spleen. The results not only provide new insights into the spleen damage and mechanisms of action of TCS and TCC but also fill the gap in toxicity data for these compounds in the juvenile stage of mammals.
